//name: The extension ID is publisher.name, so this pair reads `ffwf.tau-code`. It is not the npm scope -- an extension name may not contain `@` or `/`. The `tau-code.*` setting and command IDs below are a third namespace again, and are deliberately unchanged: renaming them would silently drop a user's settings.
name: tau-code
//displayName: A FOURTH namespace, and the only global one: `name` is scoped by publisher, so `ffwf.tau-code` is ours as soon as we own `ffwf`, but a display name is unique across the entire Marketplace and no publisher prefix applies. `tau` was refused as taken. This one matches every other identifier here -- the repository, the extension name, the .vsix. Open VSX enforces no such rule.
description: Run a tau agent inside VS Code or VSCodium.
//private: `private` stops an accidental `npm publish`. It does not stop a marketplace publish: scripts/publish-extension.sh publishes the built .vsix by path, and vsce reads the manifest out of the archive rather than off disk.
//packaging: What lands in the .vsix is controlled by .vscodeignore. vsce refuses to accept both that and a `files` property, so there is no `files` here.
//extensionKind: `workspace` so the agent's tools run where the code is -- over SSH, in WSL, in a devcontainer -- rather than on the laptop. The webview always renders locally regardless, which is the split a standalone web app cannot reproduce.

tau-code.binary.description: Path to tau's console script. A bare name is looked up on PATH.

tau-code.model.description: Passed to tau as --model. Empty uses tau's own configured default.

tau-code.provider.description: Passed to tau as --provider. Empty uses tau's own configured default.

tau-code.sessionDir.markdownDescription:
Where session logs are written (`--session-dir`).

Empty uses tau's default for RPC hosts: a private `<tmp>/.tau-<uid>/sessions`, so this extension does not fill the session list you see in the TUI. **Those sessions do not survive a reboot on a system that clears its temp directory.**

Set this to `~/.tau/sessions` to share one store with the tau TUI and `tau -p`. The two are then fully interchangeable in both directions: this extension can resume a session the TUI wrote, and the TUI's `--continue` resumes one written here.

//package: --no-dependencies because esbuild bundles everything into dist/extension.js: without it vsce walks the workspace-hoisted ../../node_modules and fails on a path outside the extension.
